environment.peak: Local Steam installation used for the native runtime tests

implementation.hud_and_models: Explicit presentation policy excludes native death, incapacitation, native controls, loading and ending screens, including live flags before ownership catches up.
implementation.placed_minecraft_blocks: World block visibility is independent of first-person HUD/avatar presentation.
implementation.local_body_and_corpses: Only the local character and its registered native skeleton/statue renderers are hidden during Minecraft-mode incapacitation. Exact previous forceRenderingOff values are restored.
implementation.native_hooks: Void postfixes observe original skeleton spawn/reassignment and statue creation after the native methods complete. Registration is filtered by local ownership before hierarchy lookup.
implementation.physics: The presentation change does not freeze, move or remove native characters/corpses, alter forces, or replace death and revival rules.
implementation.remote_scope: Remote-character filtering is covered by isolated tests. A real session between two PCs has not been completed.

native_corpse_discovery.method: Source review and linked production-hook/registry tests
native_corpse_discovery.capture: Register renderer references after native creation/assignment callbacks, including inactive and detached statue pieces.
native_corpse_discovery.steady_state: Renderer checks occur once in LateUpdate and set the flag only when needed.

overlay_resources.method: Tests link the production Overlay class to a simulated native texture/upload boundary.

optimization_verification.limitation: Deterministic boundary counters and source changes establish the removed work; they do not establish a universal real-game FPS increase.

native_death_and_owned_corpse_visibility.visual_observation: The native death screen was visible without the Minecraft HUD, first-person hand or local native skeleton. The placed cobblestone remained visible.

native_passout_and_recovery.screenshot_scope: Automatic recovery after native passout, not the separate diagnostic revival after death.

revival_and_minecraft_hud_return.limitation: This is not a two-PC cooperative revival test. The original skeleton remains a native scene object and its visibility is restored after revival; this change does not create an animated Minecraft corpse.

petrified_statue_and_fragments.scope: The installed native association fields and detached-piece API were checked locally. The production hook is compiled and covered by isolated tests; genuine petrification was not exercised in this runtime round.

scope_limitations: The native PEAK game supplies its original world and campaign; pending campaign coverage is a test limitation, not missing game content.
This change hides local native death visuals; it does not implement an animated Minecraft corpse.
Native death, camera, incapacitation and revival mechanics are retained.
No guarantee for every map, state, item, third-party mod or multiplayer condition.
Not a claim of zero bugs or complete performance optimization.
Owned native corpse visibility is restored after revival; the original scene object and its native interactions are retained.
privacy: Selected own-code test messages and measurements only. No raw game logs, account identifiers, private paths, user saves, videos, proprietary geometry or source are included.

shutdown_observation.caught_managed_cleanup_warning: Object reference not set to an instance of an object.
